root_cause.text: drm_gem_fb_init_with_funcs() uses plain integer division instead of DIV_ROUND_UP() when calculating sub-sampled plane dimensions, causing inconsistency with framebuffer_check() validation and resulting in integer underflow when computing minimum GEM object sizes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that the vulnerable code performs plain division (`mode_cmd->width / (i ? info->hsub : 1)`) while the ioctl-level framebuffer_check() uses drm_format_info_plane_width/height() which employ DIV_ROUND_UP(). For NV12 with vsub=2 and 1-pixel height, plain division yields 0 instead of 1, causing the subsequent expression `(height - 1)` to wrap to UINT_MAX as an unsigned integer, leading to min_size overflow and bypassing the GEM object size guard. The fix replaces the open-coded divisions with the helper functions that use DIV_ROUND_UP() to match the validation logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extract plane dimension calculations into dedicated helper functions to improve code maintainability and reduce duplication of subsampling logic.
intent_record.what: Replaced inline division calculations for plane width and height with calls to helper functions drm_format_info_plane_width() and drm_format_info_plane_height().
intent_record.how: Instead of manually computing plane dimensions using conditional division by horizontal/vertical subsampling factors (hsub/vsub), the code now delegates this calculation to dedicated helper functions. This centralizes the logic for plane dimension computation and ensures consistent handling of format-specific subsampling across the codebase.

Author: Noralf Trønnes <noralf@tronnes.org>

    drm: Add GEM backed framebuffer library
    
    This library provides helpers for drivers that don't subclass
    drm_framebuffer and are backed by drm_gem_object. The code is
    taken from drm_fb_cma_helper.
    
    Signed-off-by: Noralf Trønnes <noralf@tronnes.org>
    Reviewed-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch>
    Reviewed-by: Eric Anholt <eric@an
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable code is present in the drm_gem_fb_create_with_funcs() function at lines 147-148. When calculating sub-sampled plane dimensions, the code uses plain integer division: 'unsigned int width = mode_cmd->width / (i ? info->hsub : 1)' and 'unsigned int height = mode_cmd->height / (i ? info->vsub : 1)'. This is the vulnerable construct identified in the root cause. The code should use DIV_ROUND_UP() instead to match the validation logic in framebuffer_check() and prevent integer underflow when computing minimum GEM object sizes. The min_size calculation at lines 156-158 then uses these truncated dimensions, which can result in underestimated buffer size requirements. The fix is not present in this commit - it only uses plain division operators without rounding up.
